wsl-claude, transport/R19.2 in plain words (mine to do).
WHAT: a few tests look at the log FILE directly instead of asking the log. queueRestart.js:52 and liveFrontDoor.js:88 read traffic.jsonl's lines; measureCapacity.js:322 weighs the file. After the move there's no file to read, so they'd break, or worse, pass while seeing nothing. That happened once already: liveFrontDoor.js:71-79 records seven checks that 'asserted things about a log they never saw' because they read an old file that was always empty.
WHY IT'S BEFORE THE MOVE: so the move can't turn the tests red for the wrong reason, or quietly green. The two readers switch to the log's own read(), which works the same before and after; measureCapacity needs a small decision (a 'how big is the log' answer from the log itself).
DONE MEANS: all green, no test names traffic.jsonl any more (except arrivals.js's old-format fixture, which tests the one-time import on purpose), and a check that each one FAILS when handed an empty log, so none can pass blind again.

R19.2 in plain words. WHAT: four tests open the log file themselves instead of asking the log: liveFrontDoor.js:88, queueRestart.js:52, measureCapacity.js:322, plus arrivals.js:391, which writes the old file as a fixture. Once the log lives in the database, that file stops growing, so those tests would read a stale file and pass or fail for the wrong reason. They switch to asking the log (its read()), which then works wherever the rows live. WHY IT'S HERE: it blocks the move, because the harness is how we know the move broke nothing. A test reading the old file would be watching an empty room. One piece needs your decision: measureCapacity measures the file's size per entry, and README/CAPACITY.md reports that number. After the move it measures the table's pages instead. wsl-claude does this item.
